# Unit 5 historical timeline

public-student | All competition levels

Dates identify events, not an entire discovery compressed into one moment. Approximate ranges are intentional. Contextual contributors appear only where needed to explain the eight required scientists.

| Date | Scientist | Event and significance | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| c.1760–1762 | Joseph Black | Development and presentation of specific/latent heat ideas Temperature alone does not measure thermal transfer. | H01,H02 |
| 1803 | Black / editor John Robison | Posthumous collected lectures published Publication is later than the work and Black’s death. | H02 |
| 1824 | Sadi Carnot | Book on motive power of heat Reversible-engine reasoning within a caloric framework. | H06 |
| 1834 | Émile Clapeyron | Reformulation of Carnot’s work A documented route for transmission of ideas; not one of the eight required scientists. | H06 |
| 1840s | James Prescott Joule | Mechanical and thermal experiments Work and thermal effects are quantitatively related. | H05 |
| 1848 | William Thomson / Kelvin | Absolute thermometric-scale proposal An early proposal, not the final modern Kelvin definition. | H03 |
| 1850 | Rudolf Clausius | Mechanical theory of heat paper Reconciles engine reasoning with heat-work conversion. | H07 |
| 1860 | James Clerk Maxwell | Gas distribution papers A population of molecular velocities replaces one common speed. | H10 |
| 1865 | Rudolf Clausius | Entropy named and defined Developed over preceding years; distinct from energy. | H07 |
| 1867 / 1871 | James Clerk Maxwell | Demon privately described / publicly discussed Thought experiment probes microscopic control and boundaries. | H14 |
| 1877 | Ludwig Boltzmann | Probability and entropy paper Statistical interpretation of thermal behavior. | H12 |
| 1900 | Max Planck | Radiation theory and energy elements Beginning of quantum theory, not the completed photon picture. | H08,H09 |
| 1905 | Albert Einstein | Light-quantum development Later contribution distinguished from Planck; contextual name. | H09 |
| 1918 | Max Planck | Nobel Prize in Physics Recognition of earlier work, not the discovery date. | H08 |

## Read the sequence critically
Black precedes the mature energy theory. Carnot precedes Joule’s experimental program. Clausius’s macroscopic entropy precedes Boltzmann’s statistical interpretation. Planck’s 1900 work precedes his 1918 award. Do not reorder these events to match a modern textbook’s chapter order. Source IDs resolve in U5-sources.md.
